text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English monarch HENRY VIII, famous for his six wives and his rebellion against the Roman Catholic church, was born in 1491.
French philosopher JEAN-JACQUES ROUSSEAU was born in 1712.
The man who gave us the ARCHIBALD art prize was born in 1856. J.F. ARCHIBALD was editor of the Bulletin magazine.

Australian film pioneer EDWARD CARROL was born in 1868. With his brother DAN, he produced "Lure Of The Bush", "Man From Kangaroo" and "On Our Selection". He also built the Prince Edward Theatre in Sydney.
American producer, writer and director MEL BROOKS was born in 1926. His works include "The Producers".
British drummer BOBBY HARRISON, an original member of the group 'Procol Harum', was born in 1943.
British guitarist DAVE KNIGHTS, who played with 'Procol Harum' until 1969 (and played on their big hit "A Whiter Shade Of Pale"), was born in 1945.
** EVENTS **
1880 : NED KELLY fought it out in the famous siege
of Glenrowan.
1902 : The United States authorised the construction
of the Panama Canal
1914 : The event occurred that would lead to the
First World War. In Sarajevo, a 19 year-old student assassinated Archduke FRANZ FERDINAND and his wife. FRANZ was the heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne.
1919 : Germany signed the peace treaty officially
ending the First World War. The Germans considered the terms of the treaty particularly harsh in the demands for massive reparations.
1969 : The rock musical "Hair" had its first
performance in Sydney. The production, which involved nudity, prompted a moral outcry.
1979 : OPEC agreed to a 15 percent oil price rise.
1982 : PRINCE CHARLES and DIANA named their week-old
first son "WILLIAM ARTHUR PHILIP LOUIS". Their second son was born 2 years later. He was named "HENRY CHARLES ALBERT DAVID".
1984 : After more than 104 years of publication, the
British magazine "Titbits" closed its doors.
1990 : In an effort to keep the streets clean,
authorities in Florence decreed that all horses within city limits must wear underwear.
1990 : PRINCE CHARLES broke his arm when he fell
from his polo pony during a match.
1994 : PRINCE CHARLES admitted in a British
television documentary that he'd been unfaithful to PRINCESS DIANA, once it had become clear that their marriage was doomed.
